title: Toward a digital twin of the ICU patient: Forecasting and treatment response in a generative event model
abstract: arXiv:2611.27028v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A digital twin of a patient in intensive care would forecast the patient's course and what a treatment would change. Generative event models, trained to continue a patient's electronic health record (EHR), have been proposed as a path toward such twins. We trained TWICE, a 79M-parameter decoder-only transformer, on the ICU records of one academic health system (127,332 training patients and 1.57 billion tokens). We evaluated it on clinical prediction tasks, generation fidelity, individual trajectories and counterfactual validation. Reading 19 clinical outcomes off 50 simulated futures, with no task-specific training, TWICE matched the best of 144 supervised configurations on held-out patients (mean AUROC 0.836 vs. 0.834). It led on events that change care within a day and trailed on death. With the training data fixed, more and longer simulated futures were worth more than a 6.8-fold larger model. Its generated records matched real ones

translated_title: 迈向ICU患者的数字孪生：生成式事件模型中的病情预测与治疗反应
translated_abstract: 重症监护病房（ICU）患者的数字孪生应能预测患者的病情走向以及某项治疗将带来的改变。生成式事件模型——即经过训练以延续患者电子健康记录（EHR）的模型——被视为实现此类数字孪生的一条途径。我们在一个学术医疗系统的ICU记录上训练了TWICE，一个7900万参数的仅解码器（decoder-only）transformer模型（训练数据包含127,332名患者、15.7亿个token）。我们在临床预测任务、生成保真度、个体轨迹和反事实验证等方面对其进行了评估。在没有任何任务特定训练的情况下，通过从50个模拟的未来轨迹中读取19项临床结果，TWICE在留出患者上的表现与144个监督学习配置中的最佳者相当（平均AUROC 0.836 对比 0.834）。它在一天内会改变诊疗决策的事件预测上领先，而在死亡预测上表现稍逊。在训练数据固定的情况下，生成更多且更长的模拟未来，其收益超过了将模型规模扩大6.8倍。其生成的记录与真实记录相匹配……
tldr: 研究者训练了7900万参数的生成式事件模型TWICE，无需任务特定训练即可通过模拟50条患者未来轨迹，在19项ICU临床结局预测上达到与144个监督模型最佳配置相当的性能，是实现ICU患者数字孪生的重要一步。
en_tdlr: The authors trained TWICE, a 79M-parameter generative event model that continues patients' ICU EHR trajectories, showing that without any task-specific training, reading 19 clinical outcomes from 50 simulated futures matches the best of 144 supervised configurations (mean AUROC 0.836 vs. 0.834), marking a key step toward a digital twin of the ICU patient.
